solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Modifying Tredegar flat, he produces a ruler

indicators.note: modifying means changing, so the letters of the three words that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone renovates a flat in the Welsh town of Tredegar and thereby comes up with a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Modifying' rearranges TREDEGARFLATHE. Tredegar is a town in South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: The ninth-century king of Wessex is one of England's most celebrated rulers.

clue.text: In state of hostility Grandad gets war wound

indicators.note: read as the past of wind, twisted, so the letters of these three words are wound into a new order

explanation.surface: An old man is injured in combat, during a time of enmity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' looks like an injury but is the past tense of wind: the letters of GRANDADGETSWAR are twisted round.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes two parties openly hostile, as if blades were already unsheathed.

clue.text: A pivotal point in securing a purchase

definitions.text: A pivotal point in securing a purchase

parts.words: A pivotal point in securing a purchase
parts.note: purchase here means mechanical grip or leverage, and the point a lever turns on is what gives it; the surface pretends it is a key moment in a shop deal

explanation.surface: The decisive moment in closing a sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purchase' is leverage, not buying; 'pivotal' is literal, the point on which a lever pivots.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the support a lever turns on, which lets it grip and exert force.

clue.text: English see eye to eye only briefly? That's a bore

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: to see eye to eye is to agree

explanation.surface: A question about whether the English agree only for a moment, followed by a dismissive verdict that it is tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only briefly' trims AGREE to AGRE. 'bore' is not a tedious thing but a tidal wave running up a river.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagre is a tidal bore, the surge of water up an estuary such as the Severn or Trent.

clue.text: Cask remains at home, opened by a North African

parts.note: a tun is a large cask for wine or beer
remains in the sense of 'still is', so it gives IS

indicators.note: the word for at home is split open with the letter A placed inside

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: A barrel stays in the house until someone from North Africa opens it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remains' just means 'is' (still is), not leftovers.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Tunisia is a native of a North African country.

clue.text: Former eastern politician getting the first of these free

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: the first of picks the opening letter of the word these

explanation.surface: An ex-MP from the east is released from obligations before anyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: To be exempt is to be free of a duty or charge that applies to others.

clue.text: The banker's craft?

parts.note: a banker here is a river, which has banks, and its craft is a vessel sailing on it, not a financier's skill

explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is crossword slang for a river (it has banks), and 'craft' is a boat rather than a skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat built for navigating rivers is a vessel of the waterway with banks.

clue.text: Jittery head of athletics with intelligence about team

indicators.note: head of takes the first letter of athletics
about means around, so the word for intelligence is placed around the team

parts.note: nous is common sense or intelligence
XI is eleven, a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: A nervous athletics captain who is clever about the squad.
explanation.walkthrough: XI is the Roman numeral eleven, the size of a football or cricket side; 'about' signals the wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Jittery and anxious are synonyms for nervous and worried.

clue.text: In part of hospital, supporter like Ivan — a horror!

indicators.note: In puts the supporter inside the hospital department

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital
a fan is a supporter
the Russian tsar was Ivan the Terrible

explanation.surface: A fan on a hospital ward who resembles a tyrannical tsar is dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals the insertion into the Ear, Nose and Throat department. Ivan IV of Russia is known as Ivan the Terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase describes a shocking, unruly person, literally a terrible child: a horror.

clue.text: Old coach's steady application

definitions.meaning: a horse-drawn public stagecoach, especially in France

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a French stagecoach of old and careful, persistent hard work.

clue.text: Restrained by cleric, one cross, spiteful woman

indicators.note: restrained by means held within, so the letters for one and cross go inside the cleric

parts.note: Ven, for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon
I is the Roman numeral one
X is a cross shape

explanation.surface: A clergyman holding back a single angry, malicious woman.
explanation.walkthrough: VEN, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon in the Church of England; 'cross' is the letter X, not angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides a female fox, the word is used for a quarrelsome, ill-tempered woman.

clue.text: Lovely, not old, American, stuff

indicators.note: not means leave out, so the letters for old and American are taken away

parts.note: gorgeous means lovely
US stands for American, the United States

explanation.surface: A list of adjectives and a noun, like a description of fine American goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes O and US from GORGEOUS. 'stuff' is the verb, to cram in food.
explanation.definitionFit: To gorge is to stuff yourself greedily with food.

clue.text: Star beginning to undertake a month in South Africa

indicators.note: in places the run of letters inside the abbreviation for South Africa
beginning to takes the first letter of undertake

parts.note: per means a, as in 'ten pounds a head'
Nov is short for November

explanation.surface: A celebrity starting to take on a month-long stint in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' gives PER (as in 'twice per month').
explanation.definitionFit: A supernova is a star that explodes and briefly becomes enormously bright.

clue.text: The writer returned barking mad? Hard cheese!

indicators.note: returned means turned back, so the two letters for the writer read backwards

parts.note: the writer is the setter, referring to themself as me
barking mad means crazy, mental

explanation.surface: A writer comes back crazed, and someone responds with the British slang for bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard cheese!' sounds like the British slang for 'tough luck', but here means a firm cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: This Swiss cheese with holes is a hard cheese, firm enough to slice.

clue.text: Disgusted character sitting outside entrance to Ashmolean

indicators.note: outside means the Greek letter goes around the opening letter of Ashmolean

parts.note: nu is a Greek letter, a character of that alphabet

indicators.note: entrance to takes the first letter of Ashmolean

parts.note: seated means sitting

explanation.surface: Someone revolted sits outside the door of the Oxford museum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' is NU, a Greek letter. 'outside' puts NU around A. The Ashmolean is a museum in Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling sickened by something is being disgusted by it.

clue.text: Indulge group surrounding the senior officer?

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer; the group surrounding him is the CO's, giving COS
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A question whether the circle of people around a commander should be pampered.
explanation.walkthrough: The group surrounding the commanding officer is the CO's set: CO'S + SET.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosset someone is to pamper or spoil them, to indulge their every wish.

clue.text: Hiss new cricket side given Swinburne's name?

parts.note: Alger Hiss was the American official accused of being a Soviet spy
the on side is one half of a cricket field, also called leg side

explanation.surface: A poet's name is given to a new cricket team, which is hissed at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hiss' is Alger Hiss, US official accused of spying for the Soviets. In cricket the field is split into the off side and the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian poet's full name was Algernon Charles Swinburne.

clue.text: Gradually increase backing for disheartened stooges

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse
disheartened means losing its heart, the middle letter

parts.note: puppets are stooges, people controlled by others

explanation.surface: Supporting despondent sidekicks should be ramped up slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes the central P of PUPPETS, leaving PUPETS; 'backing for' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something by degrees, like production or effort, is to ramp it up step by step.

clue.text: Flag raised by one reigning over a small African state

indicators.note: raised means lifted up, so in a down entry the word for flag reads upwards

parts.note: to flag is to tire

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the two letters for a ruler are reversed

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A flag hoisted by a monarch over a small nation in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' is the verb, to tire, which 'raised' reverses to ERIT; 'over' turns ER (Elizabeth Regina) to RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eritrea is a small country on the Red Sea coast of the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: Line adopted by stout ship's officer, one sharing accommodation

indicators.note: adopted by means taken in, so the line letter goes inside the word for stout

parts.note: stout means fat
a mate is an officer on a merchant ship

explanation.surface: A portly ship's officer takes up a line and shares a cabin.
explanation.definitionFit: A flatmate is a person who shares a flat with you.

clue.text: Drivers adopting measure of speed run over upturned jar

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the drivers' letters go round everything else

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, the British motoring organisation
mph is miles per hour

indicators.note: upturned means turned upside down, so in a down entry these two letters read upwards

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Motorists measuring their speed knock over a jar.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is the Automobile Association, a British drivers' club. 'upturned' reverses RO to OR.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphora is a two-handled ancient Greek or Roman storage jar.

clue.text: Possible Afghan way to crush a rebellion at last

parts.note: a path is a way

indicators.note: at last takes the final letter of rebellion

explanation.surface: An Afghan seeking a way to put down an uprising, finally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possible' signals an example: a Pathan is one kind of Afghan.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathan is an older name for a Pashtun, a people of Afghanistan and Pakistan, so one might well be an Afghan.

clue.text: Repeat ceremony involving European count

indicators.note: involving means including, so the European letter goes inside the ceremony

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony
to rate is to count or reckon

explanation.surface: Do the ritual again, this time with a European nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'count' looks like a nobleman, but is the verb, to rate.
explanation.definitionFit: To reiterate is to say or do something again.

clue.text: Runner given work in the French Resistance

indicators.note: in places the work inside the French article

parts.note: le is French for the
op is short for opus, a work
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A messenger assigned a mission in the French Resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the French Resistance' looks like the wartime movement but splits into LE and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A loper is one who runs with a long, bounding stride.

clue.text: Trusty texter's amused response young adult initially received

indicators.note: received means taken in, so the initials go inside the texting abbreviation

parts.note: LOL, laugh out loud, is a texter's reply to something funny

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of young and adult

explanation.surface: A faithful friend gets an amused text from a youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone trusty is reliable and faithful, staying true to friends.

clue.text: Best to drop round for high-class German meat product

indicators.note: to drop means to let go, so the round letter is dropped from the word for best
for here means in exchange for, so the high-class letter takes the dropped letter's place

parts.note: to best someone is to worst them, defeat them
O is round in shape
U is the abbreviation for upper class

explanation.surface: It is better to give up a round of drinks for some fancy German sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' is the verb, to defeat, which is WORST. U means upper class in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Wurst is German sausage, a meat product.

clue.text: Structure in which workers build the cells?

definitions.text: Structure in which workers build the cells?

parts.words: Structure in which workers build the cells?
parts.note: the workers are worker bees and the cells are the wax compartments they make, not prison cells built by labourers

explanation.walkthrough: 'workers' are worker bees, and 'cells' are wax hexagons, not a prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees build this wax framework of hexagonal compartments to hold honey and larvae.

clue.text: Paid holiday assigned, interrupted by forest fire

indicators.note: interrupted by means broken into, so the forest and fire go inside the word for assigned

parts.note: gave means assigned
Arden is the forest of Shakespeare's As You Like It
an ingle is a fire on a hearth

explanation.surface: Paid time off is handed out, then a forest fire breaks out.
explanation.walkthrough: The Forest of Arden is in Warwickshire and is the setting of As You Like It; 'ingle' is an old word for a hearth fire.
explanation.definitionFit: This British term means suspension from work on full pay during a notice period, ironically called a holiday.
